items.stem: Explain why a parallelogram that is not a rectangle or rhombus has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.
items.answer: A half turn about the intersection of its diagonals maps it onto itself, but folding along any line does not.
items.markingKey: Diagonals bisect each other → order 2; no fold line matches sides and angles.

items.stem: In one line: why is every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB equidistant from A and B?
items.answer: The bisector is the set of points where the two arcs of equal radius from A and B meet, so distances to A and B are equal by construction.

items.stem: Describe how to construct a 60° angle and then a 30° angle.
items.answer: With centre at the vertex draw an arc; with the same radius from where it cuts the arm cut the arc again; join to get 60°. Bisect this angle for 30°.

items.stem: Describe how to construct a triangle with sides 4, 5, 6 cm and locate the point equidistant from all three vertices.

items.stem: Construct a regular hexagon inside a circle of radius 3 cm. Explain why stepping the radius around the circle works.
items.answer: Mark 6 arcs of radius 3 cm around the circle and join. It works because the centre and two adjacent vertices form an equilateral triangle (central angle 60°), so each side equals the radius.
